# Same-model review

**Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.**

## Correctness

**PASS.** The source paper explicitly states that its entropy-based interface state is obtained by minimizing the ideal-gas mathematical entropy over the rectangle generated by the two neighboring densities and pressures, and then claims that convexity reduces the minimization to the four vertices. It subsequently implements the four-corner comparison in Algorithm 1.

For
\[
\eta_C(\rho,p)=\frac{\rho}{\gamma-1}
(\gamma\log\rho-\log p-C),
\]
direct differentiation gives a positive-definite Hessian for every positive \(\rho,p\), but also gives \(\partial_p\eta_C<0\). Hence the rectangle minimizer lies at the larger pressure. The remaining one-dimensional derivative has a unique zero at
\[
r_C=e^{-1+C/\gamma}p_+^{1/\gamma},
\]
and strict convexity gives the projected minimizer. The excess identity reduces to the standard nonnegative function \(x\log x-x+1\). These facts prove that an interior-in-density minimum occurs on an open set of rectangles.

The two-corner reduction follows from strict monotonicity in pressure. Subtracting the two endpoint values gives the identric-mean crossover exactly. The gauge argument is also exact: changing the additive constant in specific entropy adds a multiple of the conserved mass density to the entropy density and the corresponding mass flux to the entropy flux, leaving the entropy-pair structure and Hessian unchanged while changing raw entropy differences between states of unequal density.

A standalone standard-library artifact checks the displayed counterexample, the gauge crossover, the excess identity, and 50 deterministic random rectangles against dense grids. The numerical checks support but are not used in place of the analytic proof.

## Originality

**PASS, to the best of our knowledge.** The 2026 source paper contains the rectangle-minimization claim and the four-corner implementation but does not give the exact continuous minimizer, distinguish the continuous and discrete problems, reduce the four corners to two analytically, derive the identric crossover, or discuss the dependence of the selector on the additive entropy normalization.

Older Euler literature establishes the family of convex entropy densities and explicitly records that specific entropy is determined only up to an additive constant. Those facts are prior work and are used here only to assess the invariance of the new selector. The identric mean itself is classical.

Searches by the source title and arXiv identifier, by the phrases describing entropy minimization over the density-pressure rectangle and corner reduction, by entropy-normalization/gauge terminology, and by equivalent scalar minimization formulations found no inspected correction or prior statement of the formulas in this record. No specific inaccessible paper was identified as likely to contain the same correction. Because the motivating preprint is extremely recent, contemporaneous or not-yet-indexed follow-up work remains a residual originality risk.

## Value

**PASS.** The result identifies a concrete mathematical error in the justification of a newly proposed numerical interface-state construction and replaces the stated continuous subproblem by an exact constant-cost solution. It also separates two interpretations that should not be conflated: continuous entropy minimization over a rectangle and the discrete four-corner heuristic actually implemented in the source. The gauge-dependence theorem exposes a reproducibility/invariance issue that persists even if the method is interpreted purely as a corner heuristic.

The result does not claim that the published ELCD experiments fail. Its value is as a sharp correction and design constraint: any future use of “minimum entropy” as an absolute state-ranking rule should specify the entropy normalization or use an invariant criterion, and any claim of continuous minimization should allow interior density minimizers.

## Limitations and residual risks

The exact formula is for the ideal-gas entropy used in the source paper. A corrected continuous minimizer supplies density and pressure only; because entropy is velocity-independent, it does not by itself specify a complete interface state. No replacement velocity rule or new Euler simulation is evaluated here. The existing corner heuristic might still be empirically advantageous for reasons unrelated to exact rectangle minimization. Near-vacuum regularization, floating-point tie behavior, and the performance of gauge-invariant alternatives are not analyzed.
